paragraphs.text: Praying by them rather than by words, mine afflictions having swollen my heart too big for my mouth. {See Trapp on "Psa 121:1"}
paragraphs.anchor: Unto thee lift I up mine eyes

paragraphs.text: For direction, defence, maintenance, mercy in time of correction, help when the service is too hard, &c.; so do our eyes wait upon the Lord our God, viz. for direction and benediction.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, as the eyes of servants

paragraphs.text: This is preces fundere, coelum tundere, misericordiam extorquere, as Tertullian hath it; to wring mercy out of God’s holy hands, by our utmost importunity.
paragraphs.anchor: Have mercy upon us, O Lord, have mercy

paragraphs.text: We are made the very scum and scorn of our proud imperious enemies. This the nature of man is very impatient of, and can hardly brook; for there is none so mean but holdeth himself worthy of some regard; and a reproachful scorn showeth an utter disrespect, which issueth from the very superfluity of malice.
paragraphs.anchor: For we are exceedingly filled with contempt

paragraphs.text: And therehence insolent and unsufferable, for κορος υβριν τικτει, ease breedeth forgetfulness, yea, it maketh men scornful and wrongful to others.
paragraphs.anchor: Our soul is exceedingly filled with the scorning of those that are at ease
